newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Birds caused Dutch plane crash in July - report.
newsitem.headline: Birds caused Dutch plane crash in July - report.

text.p: A swarm of birds caused a Belgian Hercules military transport plane to crash at Eindhoven airport in the Netherlands in July, according to an official report published on Thursday.
Thirty-four of the 41 people aboard perished in the blaze.

The report, compiled by the Dutch air force, the interior ministry and emergency services, found that up to 600 starlings and lapwings, out of view of the airport's control tower, took flight as the C-130 plane, returning members of a Dutch army brass band from Italy, came in to land on July 15.
The mass of birds smashed into the plane's cockpit and the left wing, with dozens of them ending up in the engines.
As the plane lost power and altitude, the pilot, who died in the crash, attempted to abort his landing.
But, with only one of four engines still running, the plane veered left and ploughed into a field, erupting in a fireball as its fuel tanks were ruptured.

The report criticised the emergency services and traffic control for poor communications before and after the crash. It took over 35 minutes before fire services were told that there were more than the four crew members on board the plane.
The defence ministry said that the airbase commander, duty traffic controller and fire chief had been suspended from duty pending further inquiries.
